findings.issue: The SPEC-09 import-boundary scanner only matches static `import ... from '<single-quoted>';` statements. `export { x } from '../engine/hand'`, `export * from`, dynamic `import('../engine/hand')`, side-effect imports, or a double-quoted specifier inside src/bots would not be caught. Today there is no reachable path: src/bots/tag.ts imports only PlayerView/PublicPlayer/SeatPolicy/Action types and advice/recommend, and the runner hands the policy only playerView(state, toAct) (runner.ts:147). recommend/postflop/preflop also import only PlayerView-side types from the engine.
findings.evidence: Future bot source -> `export * from '../engine/hand'` or `await import('../engine/deck')` -> regex IMPORT never matches -> SPEC-09 passes while the bot reaches engine internals. Not reachable in the current diff.
findings.fix: Optional: also match `^export\s.*from\s+['"]` and `import\(` (and accept either quote style), or rely on an ESLint no-restricted-imports rule scoped to src/bots/**.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR. The TAG bot (src/bots/tag.ts) takes a PlayerView only. It imports engine types only (Action, PlayerView, PublicPlayer, SeatPolicy) plus advice/recommend, whose engine imports are also PlayerView-side types or pure helpers (cards, hand-evaluator, seeded-random). The runner calls the policy with playerView(state, state.toAct), which builds fresh copies of the players, pots, actions and legal-action arrays and exposes only the hero's hole cards. No cast or import path reaches HandState, the deck or other players' hole cards. The equity.ts edit turns the `readonly c` parameter property into an explicit readonly field set in the constructor, so the emitted behaviour is the same. The preflop.ts `with { type: 'json' }` attribute only changes how the module loads; it does not change the imported data. tagPolicy is stateless and shared across seats, so no state leaks between seats. FREE_CHECK_EQUITY ignores the card contents and only maps over the opponent count. Resource bounds: free postflop checks now skip equity entirely. Facing-bet decisions use the existing computeEquity, which is limited to at most 9 opponents (MAX_OPPONENTS), has a feasibility node limit and falls back to a fixed 30,000-trial sample. The TAG path has no unbounded loop or recursion. There are no new dependencies, secrets, inputs, logging or randomness. One MINOR: the SPEC-09 boundary scanner does not catch re-exports or dynamic imports. I did not run any Vitest or coverage runs.
